title: LINGUAPINAS System Evaluation Questionnaire
about: Software quality evaluation based on ISO/IEC 25010. Answered in the game (Settings > EVALUATION SURVEY). Answers are saved in the game's SQLite database by survey round, so the same questionnaire can be answered again (re-survey) after the system is improved.
instructions: Read each statement and choose the number that best describes your evaluation of LINGUAPINAS.

items.text: The available functions support the main purpose of LINGUAPINAS as a Philippine-language educational game.
Menus and buttons open the screens or perform the actions indicated by their labels.
Island-group or language selection follows the rules implemented in the game.
The application responds to common user actions within an acceptable time on the test device.
Transitions between available screens occur without excessive delay.
Images, animations, and audio load or play within an acceptable time, where implemented.
The application runs in the intended operating environment used for evaluation.
The implemented scenes, controls, and media work together without interfering with one another.
Audio playback, where implemented, does not prevent users from continuing an activity.
The interface makes the main navigation options easy to identify.
Text, labels, and instructions are readable on the test device.
Buttons and interactive controls are easy to recognize and operate.
The application launches successfully in the test environment.
The main learning flow can be completed without a crash or blocking error.
Repeated use of the same function produces consistent results.
The application requests or uses only the user information needed for its implemented functions.
Player information, if collected, is not unnecessarily exposed through the interface.
Local database files or stored data, if used, are handled in a way that avoids obvious unintended exposure.
Related functions are separated clearly enough to support corrections and future updates.
The structure allows developers to understand how the main game functions are connected.
Relevant dependencies, setup requirements, and known limitations are identifiable to a developer.
The application can be configured or adjusted for its intended environment without disproportionate effort.
The project can be transferred to another compatible development or test environment using documented setup steps.
Language lessons or quiz content can be updated without changing unrelated parts, if supported by the current design.
The game provides appropriate warnings or guidance for potentially disruptive actions, where relevant.
If an error occurs, the application avoids causing avoidable loss of user progress where saving is implemented.
The application handles its implemented functions in a way that does not create an evident risk to the user or device during normal use.
